Effects by event time, cohort, period, or unit

Source: R/effects.R
trop_effects.Rd

trop_effects() averages the effects of the treated cells of a trop() fit in groups. A group is, for example, all treated cells with the same number of periods since the start of the treatment. The function can also give bootstrap standard errors, intervals, and simultaneous bands for all groups.

Usage

trop_effects(
  fit,
  by = c("event_time", "cohort", "time", "unit", "overall"),
  window = NULL,
  n_boot = NULL,
  boot_rows = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  conf_level = fit$conf.level,
  ci = c("normal", "percentile"),
  seed = NULL,
  anticipation = 0L
)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

fit

A trop object from trop() or trop_matrix() with method = "local".

by

The groups. Refer to the section Groups.

window

An optional vector with 2 event times. The function uses cells with an event time from window[1] to window[2].

n_boot

The number of new bootstrap draws. With NULL, the function uses the draws of the fit, if the fit has draws. With 0, the function does not calculate a bootstrap.

boot_rows

A matrix of draws from trop_boot_rows(). This argument replaces n_boot.

strata, resample

The settings for new draws. Refer to trop_boot_rows(). With resample = NULL, the function uses the setting of the fit.

conf_level

The confidence level. The default is the level of the fit.

ci

Use "normal" or "percentile". Refer to trop().

seed

An optional integer seed for new draws. The function does not change the state of the random number generator in the R session.

anticipation

The number of treated periods at the start of each run that come before the true start. Refer to the section Anticipation. The default 0 uses the first treated period as the start.

x

A trop_effects object.

digits

The number of significant digits to show.

...

Not used.

row.names, optional

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class trop_effects with one row for each group. The columns are the group (the name of the column is the value of by), estimate, and n_cells. With a bootstrap, the columns std.error, conf.low, conf.high, band.low, and band.high are also in the data frame. The data frame has these attributes: draws (a matrix with one column for each group), rows (the rows of the draws), and critical (the critical value of the band). When by is a list, the result is a named list of such data frames.

Details

The function uses the effects tau of the fit. Thus, the target cells of the fit are the only cells in the groups. A cell that has no effect in the fit, for example a cell outside of the target, is not in a group. A group with no such cell is not in the result.

Groups

The argument by sets the groups:

  • "event_time": the number of periods since the start of the current treatment. The value 0 is the first treated period. If a unit stops the treatment and starts it again, the count starts again.

  • "cohort": the period in which the current treatment started.

  • "time": the period.

  • "unit": the unit.

  • "overall": one group with all cells. The result is the ATT.

  • A matrix with the dimensions of the panel. The values are the group of each cell. A cell with NA is not in a group. Only treated cells with an effect are in groups.

  • A named list of the values above, for example list(event = "event_time", cohort = "cohort"). The function then gives a named list with one result for each element. All results use the same bootstrap draws, and the function calculates the estimator only one time for each draw. A character element without a name uses its value as the name.

The argument window limits the cells to cells with an event time in the window. For example, window = c(0, 3) uses the first 4 treated periods.

Anticipation

Sometimes the treatment has an effect before it starts, for example when units know the start date. A usual procedure is to set W = 1 in the periods before the start, so that these cells are not controls. Then, the first W = 1 cell is not the true start.

With anticipation = k, the function counts the first k treated periods of each run as the periods before the start. Thus, these periods get the event times -k to -1, and the event time 0 is the true start. The cohort is also the period of the true start. A cohort that starts after the last period of the panel is not in a group.

To keep the anticipation cells out of the estimate, also remove them from the target of the fit.

Inference

The bootstrap uses the unit draws of the fit. For each draw, the function calculates the local estimator again with the tuning parameters of the fit. Then it averages the effects of each group. The tuning parameters do not change. The standard error of a group is the standard deviation of its draws. A group that has no treated cell in a draw has no value for that draw.

The draws run in parallel with the threads of the control of the fit.

By default, the function uses the draws that the fit stored in fit$boot$rows. Then the average of all treated cells has the same draws as fit$boot$draws. With n_boot, the function makes new draws. With boot_rows, you give the draws. A group of one fit and a group of another fit have a joint distribution only if they use the same draws.

Each call calculates the estimator again for each draw. To get many sets of groups, give them in one list to by. To calculate the draws only one time, make the fit with se = "none". Then include "overall" in the list, and give the draws with boot_rows.

The columns band.low and band.high give a simultaneous band with the sup-t method. The band has a critical value for all groups. The critical value is a quantile of the largest absolute value of the standardized draws over the groups. The band contains all true group effects with the probability conf_level, if the bootstrap is correct.

The intervals conf.low and conf.high are for one group each. The band needs many draws. With only one group, the band columns are NA.

See also

trop_boot_rows(), trop_stepdown()

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                     n_post = 3, effect = 1, seed = 1)
fit <- trop(sim, "y", "d", "unit", "time",
            lambda = c(time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5),
            n_boot = 50, seed = 1, control = trop_control(threads = 1))
trop_effects(fit, by = "event_time")
#> TROP effects by event time
#>  event_time estimate n_cells std.error conf.low conf.high band.low band.high
#>           0  1.41712       5    0.3535   0.7243     2.110   0.6428    2.1914
#>           1  1.97684       5    0.4643   1.0669     2.887   0.9599    2.9938
#>           2 -0.03763       5    0.3825  -0.7873     0.712  -0.8755    0.8002
#> Bootstrap: 50 draws. The band is simultaneous (sup-t) at the 95% level.

# Two sets of groups with one bootstrap sweep.
both <- trop_effects(fit, by = list(event = "event_time", time = "time"))
trop_stepdown(both)
#>       name    estimate std.error          t      p_raw      p_adj
#> 1 event: 0  1.41712290 0.3534799  4.0090621 0.01960784 0.01960784
#> 2 event: 1  1.97684134 0.4642597  4.2580507 0.01960784 0.01960784
#> 3 event: 2 -0.03762763 0.3824907 -0.0983753 0.90196078 0.90196078
#> 4 time: 10  1.41712290 0.3534799  4.0090621 0.01960784 0.01960784
#> 5 time: 11  1.97684134 0.4642597  4.2580507 0.01960784 0.01960784
#> 6 time: 12 -0.03762763 0.3824907 -0.0983753 0.90196078 0.90196078
